question: Can a microbial/cyanobacteria-community proxy (incl. mcyE/ndaF toxic-strain genotype qPCR) recover leave-one-HUC-region-out transfer of the microcystin fusion (collapses to ~0.485-0.527)?
method: WQP Result service queried at the 227 fusion site IDs for community/genotype characteristics; co-located nearest +/-14 d; real HUC2 from WQP Station service.
verdict: STILL DATA-BLOCKED (structural): every co-located community/genotype characteristic exists in exactly ONE HUC2 region (mcyE/ndaF & cyano density in HUC18 only; cyano percent & algae density in HUC15 only; cyano-chla-probe in one site). Leave-one-HUC-region-out is impossible for the community modality: no community feature is present in >=2 regions, so it cannot appear in both a train and a held-out test region. The genotype key exists at fusion sites but is spatially confined (3 orgs, 2 regions), so the cross-region recovery hypothesis cannot be tested. Cross-region AUROC with the 4th modality is UNCOMPUTABLE (not >0.53, not <=0.5 — undefined).
unblock_spec: Need the SAME community/genotype characteristic (ideally Microcystin/nodularin genes mcyE/ndaF qPCR, or standardized cyanobacteria cell-count/biovolume) co-located (same site, +/-14 d of a microcystin sample) at monitoring programs in >=2 distinct HUC2 regions with both classes, e.g. >=2 regions x >=30 co-located samples x >=6 positives each. Concretely: add mcyE/qPCR at the Florida 21FL* HAB sites (bulk of fusion samples, currently zero community records) OR at Great-Lakes 21MICH/21OHIO/USGS sites. WQP already holds USGS mcyE gc/uL and NARS cyanobacteria counts, but at NON-fusion sites lacking co-located Sentinel-2 + pigment + microcystin.
